plain: To send a case back to a lower court for more action

webster.text: To call or send back him or that which is ordered to a place; as, to remand an officer from a distant place; to remand an envoy from a foreign court.

example.quote: To remand the cause for a new trial would answer no purpose.
example.cite: James Madison, Notes of Debates in the Federal Convention of 1787, June 5, 1787
